plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This holds true whether there are 2, 3, or more competitors, and doesn't depend on their strategies. Since my value is $48, bidding exactly $48 maximizes my expected profit: if I win, I pay the second-highest bid (which is what I would have paid anyway if truthful), and I never risk overpaying or leaving value on the table by shading my bid.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy. This holds regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies, since your payment depends only on the second-highest bid, not your own bid (as long as you win). Bidding above value risks winning at a loss; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my private value of $38 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction) with independent private values. In such auctions, truthful bidding (bidding exactly my value) is the dominant strategy regardless of what other rational bidders do. Bidding my true value of $12 ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid, and I never overpay since I only pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid. This maximizes expected profit.
